key_conclusions: 65K cutover is the main new event: handoff at step-372000 (95.3% of 390,251; 0.84T tokens/4.7% left; 18,251 steps), CP1×EP64, capacity factor 1.5, qk_mult 1.66; #10820 merged 2026-11-02T02:55:41Z, child launched 03:25Z, six post-switch checks passed at 04:03Z (step 372,102, agent-reported).

The 65K phase is running, not finished: median 16.05 s/step, mean drop 4.058e-4, peak HBM 127.8 GiB, control-window loss delta −0.02009 vs the 16K parent (it did not trigger the set anomaly threshold; not the same as “no jump”); projected finish ~2026-11-05T15:00Z. The source's '-15% tok/s' was a projection; measured throughput change is about −10.4% (16.05 vs 14.38 s) to −11.0% (logged tok/s).

No 65K eval result exists by 05:30Z: the first eval is expected at step 375,000 (~11-02T17:20Z) and the permanent checkpoint at 378,000 (~11-03T07:00Z); both are after the cutoff. Eval packs at the training length, so Paloma macro may step and eval_regressed (2% threshold) may fire; this is a risk, not an observed regression.

There is no long-context capability benchmark above 32K. The 65K phase is judged on loss (including held-out Paloma loss at 65K packing), not on a capability benchmark; #7638 (RULER) was auto-closed 2026-10-24.

A gradient-spike investigation (#10677) reproduced one spike exactly on the step-324000 batch at 324000 weights and pinned it to one 16K sequence/token/op; later spikes were not reproduced at their own weights. #10783 added a global gradient clip at 1.0 (merged 10-30), and the hero relaunched as hero-gradclip-step356k; the 50-step gate was GO, but the clip never fired on the hero (0/50, 0/197). It did fire in one-rack rt1/rt2 tests.

The 10-29 outage was a distinct IMEX/NCCL OOM incident: attempts 1–15 failed, attempt 16 resumed at step-352321 at 20:47:17Z after a human operator migrated to rack 399. It is not the gradient-spike event; no evidence links the two.

Eval measurement matters: an independent observer measured ~0.031 lower Paloma macro at 16K vs 4K on nearly the same weights (restored from the same checkpoint, a few extra steps); at 262K, short PTB/WikiText-103 corpora would yield zero-token tags and distort the macro. #10711 addresses this but is approved, open/dirty, and has no GPU rehearsal.

#10709 is open/blocked with one-rack 65K CP4 evidence (+7.4 GiB non-pool vs 5.8 GiB headroom, 90.49 GiB allocation failure) and no 11-rack test. #10618 is approved but dirty/unmerged, and its promised 65K CP4 rack validation never appeared. 262K has not started.
The 16K switch (#10101, 2026-10-14) and #9615 are background, not new progress in this window.
uncertainties: 65K gate numbers are agent/author-reported; W&B curves were not read and no third party re-measured the run.
The clip's effectiveness is unproven: it did not fire on the hero (0/50, 0/197) and fired only in one-rack rt1/rt2 tests; the 50-step trial proves no regression, not protection.
The 10-29 outage's exact IMEX ownership and safe-recovery procedure remain unconfirmed; attempts 10 and 14 are not logged, so the retry count cannot be fully enumerated.
The step-325710 and step-353060 spikes were never reproduced at their own weights; only the step-324000 mechanism is established. Do not generalize the single-token/op chain to 325710/353060.
The 4K re-evaluation of all checkpoints was promised for after the run finishes; no public record by 05:30Z, and it may have happened internally without a public post.
mtracker is LLM-generated and has at least two inconsistencies with GitHub ('step 372,300', 'stopped after 372,058'); its numbers were not used.

A code-only observation from #10711's patch: HERO_FIXED_EVAL_SEQ_LENS=(4096,65_536,262_144) filtered by ≤ training length would, at 65K, evaluate 4K and 65K but drop the 16K series. Authors have not discussed this; treat as an open question, not a conclusion.
